title: Do You Need A Chimney Cap? What It Does & Costs | Northmark
description: What a chimney cap does, what goes wrong without one, galvanized vs stainless, and how a cap is sized and fitted. From a WETT-certified technician in Toronto.
h1: Do You Need A Chimney Cap? What It Does, And What Happens Without One
lead: A chimney cap is the cheapest part of a chimney and the one most often missing. Here is what it actually does, the four problems we find in Toronto chimneys that have none, and what to look for when you buy one.

hero.alt: New stainless steel chimney cap with mesh screen fitted on a brick chimney in Toronto

hero_caption: A stainless cap with a mesh screen: rain, snow and animals stay out, smoke and gases get out.

sections.body:
A cap sits on top of the flue — the clay or metal pipe that runs up the middle of the chimney — and does three things at once. The lid keeps rain and snow from falling straight down the flue. The mesh screen around the sides keeps birds, squirrels and raccoons out. And the whole thing acts as a spark arrestor, stopping embers from landing on the roof.

It is not decoration, and it is not optional on a chimney that is used. An open flue is a pipe, open to the sky, that ends in your living room.

• Water in the flue. Rain and melting snow run down the flue tiles and into the smoke chamber and firebox. Over a few winters the water cracks the tiles, rusts the damper and soaks the masonry — and a wet flue mixed with creosote is where the musty smell after rain comes from.
  • Animals. Raccoons and squirrels nest on the smoke shelf; birds nest in the flue. A nest blocks the chimney, and a blocked chimney sends smoke — and carbon monoxide — back into the house. Removing a nest is a separate job, and it is not a pleasant one.
  • Debris. Leaves and twigs collect on the smoke shelf, hold moisture, and burn when the fire is lit.
  • Downdrafts. On a windy day, an open flue lets wind push straight down into the firebox. A cap breaks the wind and helps the chimney draw.

Galvanized steel caps are cheaper and rust. In Toronto's weather a galvanized cap usually shows rust within a few years, and the rust runs down the chimney and stains the brick or the crown. Then the cap is replaced, and the staining stays.

A stainless steel cap costs more once and does not rust. On a chimney you intend to keep, it is the only one worth fitting. Copper caps exist for homes where the look matters; they last as long as stainless and cost more.

sections.h2: How a cap is sized and fitted
sections.body:
A cap has to match the flue. For a single clay flue tile, the cap clamps to the outside of the tile that sticks up above the crown — so the tile has to be sound and high enough to clamp to. A chimney with two flues takes either two caps or one multi-flue cap that bolts to the crown and covers both.

Round metal liners take a cap that fits the liner's own collar. A cap that is the wrong size is either loose, and blows off in the first storm, or restricts the flue and hurts the draft. We measure the flue on the inspection and fit the cap to it.

sections.h2: When the cap is not the problem
sections.body: A missing cap is often the first thing a homeowner notices and the first thing a cheap quote offers to fix. It is worth fixing — but a new cap on a chimney with a cracked crown or open joints does not stop the water. The free inspection looks at the whole top of the chimney, from the roof, and photographs it. If the cap is all it needs, that is what we quote.

faq.q: How much does a chimney cap cost in Toronto?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the flue, whether it is a single-flue or multi-flue cap, and the material. We measure the flue on the free inspection and give you the price in writing before anything is fitted. See chimney caps.

faq.q: Can I install a chimney cap myself?
faq.a: On a single clay flue with a sound tile, a handy homeowner can — if they are comfortable on the roof and measure the flue correctly. The mistakes we see are the wrong size, a loose clamp, and a cap fitted to a tile that is already cracked.

faq.q: Does a cap affect the draft?
faq.a: A correctly sized cap improves it by stopping downdrafts. A cap that is too small, or whose mesh has clogged with creosote, restricts the flue; that is one of the things a yearly sweep checks.

faq.q: There is an animal in my chimney. What do I do?
faq.a: Do not light a fire. Keep the damper closed, and call us: we remove the nest, check the flue for damage, and fit a cap so it does not happen again.
